clue.text: Incomplete text of certificate

parts.note: a script is a written text, as of a play

explanation.definitionFit: Scrip is a certificate entitling the holder to shares or money, a financial paper.

clue.text: Made to run two editions under one impress

parts.note: a stamp is an impress or impression

indicators.note: two says the abbreviation is written twice

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for edition

explanation.surface: Printing two editions beneath a single seal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle that are stampeded are panicked into running.

clue.text: Party organised without non-mixing element

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside says the organised word encloses the party word

parts.note: to run something is to organise it
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A badly arranged party leaves out an element that will not mix.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue has a stray apostrophe; the page has none.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a noble gas, chemically inert, so it will not combine with other elements.

clue.text: Drops the artefact: the result?

indicators.note: the result asks what the clue's first words become after breaking up

explanation.surface: Someone drops an antique, and asks what is left.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop an old pot and the result is a broken shard, the very thing the shuffled letters spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A potsherd is a broken fragment of pottery, often found by archaeologists.

clue.text: Retainer making a guarded point

explanation.surface: A servant or adviser makes a cautious argument.
explanation.definitionFit: This clip holds fabric together, retaining it, and its sharp tip is covered by a guard.

clue.text: Active agent captured regiment

indicators.note: captured says the agent holds the regiment's letter inside

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
R is the abbreviation for regiment

explanation.surface: A busy secret agent took a regiment prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry means lively and nimble, especially of an older person.

clue.text: Kipling's fools were praised insincerely

explanation.surface: The foolish people in a Kipling poem were given hollow compliments.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's poem 'The Islanders' mocks 'the flannelled fools at the wicket', cricketers in white flannel trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricketers dressed in white woollen trousers; and to flatter with smooth talk is a British idiom.

clue.text: Put up with discomfort, say, of low seat

parts.note: to tough it out is to endure hardship

explanation.surface: Someone endures sitting uncomfortably on a very low stool.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in the held clue is a line break on the page. 'Tough it' spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Miss Muffet sat on one in the nursery rhyme: a small stool or grassy hummock.

clue.text: Clerk, a drug-dealer, depressed by American prison

indicators.note: depressed by puts the dealer below the prison in this down answer

parts.note: pen is short for penitentiary, a US prison
a pusher sells drugs

explanation.surface: An office worker who sells drugs is jailed in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerk doing routine paperwork is derisively called a pen-pusher.

clue.text: Simple trail originally lost by Indian

indicators.note: lost by says a letter is dropped from the Indian word

parts.note: a native of India is an Indian

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of trail

explanation.definitionFit: Naive means innocent and unsophisticated.

clue.text: Check no gas is around in the halls

parts.note: to audit is to check accounts

parts.note: air is the gas we breathe

explanation.walkthrough: 'no gas is around' reads like a safety check, but 'is around' turns AIR to RIA, and the definition is a plural of Latin form.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditoria is the Latin plural of auditorium, a large hall where an audience sits.

clue.text: Parasites have sport with soldier

parts.note: fun, as in 'in sport', means amusement
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Lice or ticks make merry with a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Many moulds and mushrooms live as parasites on plants and animals.

clue.text: Vigorous, like a shire-horse?

explanation.surface: Someone strong is compared to a big farm horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Suffolk Punch is a British breed of heavy draught horse, like a shire horse; the question mark flags the made-up sense of a horse being punch-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Forceful and energetic is the first sense; the second is a playful adjective from the Punch breed of heavy carthorse.

clue.text: Dangerous, rescue in explosion

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so these letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A rescue carried out during a blast would be risky.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsafe or unstable is dangerous, not secure.

clue.text: Enthusiasm to leave?

explanation.surface: Asking whether eagerness means departing.
explanation.definitionFit: Energy and drive is the noun; rising and departing is the literal phrase.

clue.text: Make soldier dry out from misbehaving through drink

indicators.note: out, as in 'inside out', says the letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: Drying out a soldier who has been rowdy after drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Drunk and disorderly is the charge for a person behaving badly while intoxicated.

clue.text: Sluggish part of the day, mid-evening?

indicators.note: part of says only a portion of the day's name is kept, dropping its end

parts.note: Saturday is taken as the day, the weekend day
nine o'clock is around the middle of the evening

explanation.surface: Feeling lethargic for part of the day, around the middle of the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' trims DAY from SATURDAY to leave SATUR; the question mark admits the loose reading of nine as mid-evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine, under the planet's heavy influence, means gloomy and sluggish in temperament.

clue.text: Woman married assistant zoo-keeper long ago

parts.note: she is a woman, as a pronoun

explanation.surface: A married woman once worked as a helper at the zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Shem was one of Noah's sons, who helped look after the animals on the Ark.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah's son would have helped care for the Ark's animals in ancient times, making him a keeper's helper.

clue.text: Outdated men hate to change

indicators.note: to change says these letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned men dislike any change.
explanation.definitionFit: Moth-eaten describes something worn-out and antiquated.

clue.text: Surpass with striking sports clothes

parts.note: workers out on strike are striking
a strip is a team's sports kit

explanation.surface: Outdoing others while wearing eye-catching sportswear.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrip is to outrun or exceed.

clue.text: Does one get taken out to eat?

definitions.text: Does one get taken out to eat?

parts.words: Does one get taken out to eat?
parts.note: one reading is a person invited out to dinner by a partner; the other is a fruit from a palm that gets stoned and eaten

explanation.definitionFit: A romantic outing partner and a sweet palm fruit both fit; the clue plays on both.

clue.text: 7, office pet, receiving a sovereign

clue.text: Threatened to collapse, but couldn't be demolished

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a listed building is protected from demolition by law; the full stop in the held clue is not on the page.

clue.text: Officer once famously on a charge for casual dress

definitions.text: Officer once famously on a charge

explanation.walkthrough: The Earl of Cardigan led the Charge of the Light Brigade in 1854; 'on a charge' looks like military discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earl leading a cavalry attack gave his name to the knitted woollen jacket worn informally.

clue.text: Eccentric American writer? No, French

parts.note: a cam is an eccentric, an off-centre wheel in engineering
US means American

explanation.surface: An odd American author is corrected: he was French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' looks like a description of the writer, but in engineering a cam is an eccentric wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Camus was a French novelist, author of The Outsider.

clue.text: A second dimension to the court

parts.note: size is a measurement or dimension

explanation.surface: A further measurement is taken to a legal tribunal.
explanation.walkthrough: The assizes were periodic courts held in English counties until 1972.
explanation.definitionFit: An assize was a historical session of a law tribunal.

clue.text: Gold piece, outranking others to some extent

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

clue.text: To kill insect was terribly tricky at first

indicators.note: terribly says the letters of was are badly jumbled
at first points to the opening letter of tricky

parts.note: a Maoist follows Mao Zedong's revolutionary doctrine

explanation.definitionFit: Downright means outright or plain, as in downright rude.

clue.text: Craft wished for the Bonnie Prince (without the 'Bonnie)?

parts.words: wished for the Bonnie Prince (without the 'Bonnie)?

explanation.surface: A vessel is hoped for to carry Charles Edward Stuart away.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonnie Prince Charlie fled to Skye in 1746; the Scottish song begins 'Speed, bonnie boat, like a bird on the wing'.

clue.text: Spike to fasten outside
